commands: /bin/bash -lc 'rg -n "cannot derive target-relative merge paths|target-relative merge paths|merge_worker|merge base|merge-base" app tests'

/bin/bash -lc 'rg -n "changed_paths|cannot derive target-relative|MAX.*15|TimeoutExpired|name-only" tests/test_merge* tests/test_acceptance* tests/test_merge_test_gate.py tests 2>/dev/null | head -120'
final_text:
CAUSE: `changed_paths()` applies a fixed 15-second timeout to the full `git diff --name-only <target>...HEAD` in `_git()`. On this 2,402-file branch, Git can exceed that limit while calculating the diff; `_git()` catches `TimeoutExpired` and returns `None`, which `changed_paths()` propagates. `_prepare_admission_snapshot()` then raises “cannot derive target-relative merge paths.” Retrying repeats the same bounded command, so it fails the same way.

Evidence: `app/merge_test_gate.py`, `_git()` sets `timeout=15` and converts timeouts to `None`; `changed_paths()` returns `None` when the name-only diff fails; `app/merge_operations.py`, `_prepare_admission_snapshot()` turns that result into the reported refusal. The large file count fits this failure path; the error alone does not prove the command timed out, since other Git failures also become `None`.

The missing-merge-base guess is unverified. `changed_paths()` asks Git to diff `target_sha...HEAD`, which computes the merge base; an unavailable base could also make the diff fail.

Recommended fix: distinguish timeout from Git errors in `_git()` and include the failing command in diagnostics. Give this path a timeout appropriate to large diffs, or optimize its path collection, and add a regression test for a timed-out name-only diff.
